title: Does the significant novelty in the waste fed vortices saturate? c30's cohort count against the kind-blind twin falls from ~3 to ~0.4 per 1000 t after t~5000 on seeds 3-5; a T=30000 checkpointed pair and a 1.5x box would decide it
summary: On five seeds the 3-component kind-specific-waste vortices reach more trait classes than the kind-blind twin and replace their top classes. The kinds that outgrow every new twin kind (c30's statistic) become rare late in the run (20261027T1853-c59-vortex-o-statistic, 20261027T2243-c59-trait3d-seed5-rarity). Two readings remain: real saturation, or a fixed threshold that standing diversity makes harder to reach. Before any C:open-ended claim, run longer and in a larger box. Also run a threshold scaled to the population share, which separates the two readings.
experiment: Use trait3c.py (20261027T2243-c59-trait3d-seed5-rarity, resumable every 250 t) with WORLD_DIR set to 20261027T1401-c58-vortex-trait3d. Run 2 fresh seeds, each with its own mut_seed, to T=30000. Each seed needs a waste arm (sw 0.4) and a twin (sw 0); 1 thread each takes ~4 h per pair, and the runs can be split across loops. Then run SIZE=192 with mut_dt 22 to T=10000. Score with o_vortex.py, plus a share-normalised a* (activity / population), and report significant new kinds per 2000 t in both arms.
